# Figure 1: Defining the problem

::: {#fig-figure-1}

Overview of the multispecific cell-type-selectivity problem and the experimental and computational framework used to evaluate candidate receptor targets.
:::

## Outline

* Number of combinations to consider is huge: pairs/triads of receptors, all cell populations
* Methods of increasing complexity and computational cost:
  + Target/off-target distribution shape
  + KL divergence
  + W distance
  + The binding model.
* The experimental framework:
  + CITE-seq approximates surface protein expression at single-cell resolution
  + We define a set of possible surface targets pairs and target cell types
  + Some surface proteins are lowly expressed and have higher expression in off-target cells than target cells. These are filtered on a per-target-cell-type basis
  + For every target pair/target cell type combination, we evaluate selectivity based on EMD, KL divergence, and binding model
